title: Next.js 16 Data Fetching And Caching Questionnaire

questions.prompt: A request is deduped during one render pass. What can you conclude?

options.label: It is now persistently cached across requests.
Only the current render avoided duplicate work unless a persistent cache was also configured.
The CDN will serve the same response to all users.

questions.explanation: Request memoization, persistent framework cache, browser cache, and CDN cache are different layers.

questions.prompt: Fill the product term that must be named before caching.
questions.template: Before caching a read, name the acceptable {{blank}} for users.
questions.explanation: Caching is a product contract about acceptable staleness, not only a performance trick.

questions.prompt: Match the cache layer to the risk.

pairs.match: dedupes duplicate work inside one render

questions.explanation: Debugging stale data starts by locating the layer that served the stale response.

questions.prompt: When is no-store behavior the best answer?

options.label: When nobody understands which cache is stale.
When data cannot be safely reused and must be read fresh per request.
For every dashboard because dashboards are always dynamic.

questions.explanation: No-store is right for genuinely unreusable data, not as a substitute for finding a bad cache key.
